candidate_sources.README.md:
# Harbor sonar inspection upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Go 1.13.8.
Dependencies: Go standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

checkpoints: A warm panel source delivers its synchronous cached packet as initial visible progress and remains subscribed for later packets.
Immediate and deferred packet decodes retain their existing recordProgress effect.
If a newer-received full frame is displayed before an older-received frame finishes decoding, the older completion does not roll back the display.
A later-received frame may display a lower or reset loaded value.
Navigation during synchronous startup does not let resumed older startup work displace the newer visit or continue painting the retired visit.
Navigation from recordProgress or showProgress preserves current-visit authority and display freshness.
Retry remains within its visit, retains existing cancellation, record, notice, and attempt behavior, and shares that visit's display freshness.
Hide, replacement, disposal, repeated cancellation, and repeated listener removal retain existing behavior.
Selecting the same file object later creates a distinct working visit.
Queue records remain exactly {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
Telemetry retains its current live-delta behavior and start/listen ordering.
After an Action, run a public Go syntax/build check with generated artifacts outside /workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not change public transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, notice, queue-record, Snapshot, or Client behavior beyond changes necessary for the requested panel repair.
Do not add byteCount or any other queue-record field.
Do not suppress recordProgress solely because its frame is ineligible for display.
Do not use loaded magnitude to determine frame freshness.
Do not let an older frame replace a newer-received frame that has already been displayed.
Do not let retired startup or cleanup work overwrite ownership established by newer navigation.
Do not apply the panel bootstrap or full-frame display policy to Telemetry.
Do not weaken ordinary streaming, cancellation idempotence, repeated listener removal, disposal, or later reuse.
Do not modify tests or configuration or place generated binaries, classes, or caches in /workspace.
lifecycle_identity: Each Select creates a distinct visit identified by the session serial, including repeated selection of the same File object.
Retry keeps the current visit and file but creates a new physical attempt with a new session-local attempt number.
A decoded frame's audit payload retains the file and attempt captured by enqueue.
Visible progress is authorized by the originating Visit object being the session's current visit, not merely by a matching file ID or token.
Because retry does not create a visit and freshness concerns the current display, the display-order state is associated with the visit and spans its attempts.
Each Session owns independent serial, attempt, visit, task, and disposal state.
The concrete mechanism for coordinating a listener whose start call has not returned is an implementation choice.

obligations.text: For panel attempts with Feed enabled, arrange reception so packets emitted synchronously by start can produce the initial progress update, while preserving reception of later streaming packets.

Coordinate panel startup with navigation and cleanup so synchronous showProgress navigation during start cannot allow older resumed startup work to replace newer visit ownership or continue visible output for a retired visit.
Assign panel packet freshness by reception order before decoding, since decoding may finish immediately or later and completion order may differ from reception order.
Preserve the existing audit-before-view behavior for each decode completion: recordProgress uses the originating fileId and attemptId even when the frame is later denied visible publication.
After audit callbacks return, display a frame only if its originating visit is still current and it is not older than a newer-received frame already published for that visit.
Commit the visit's publication ordering before invoking showProgress so synchronous reentrant delivery cannot later restore an older display state.
Use reception order rather than loaded values for freshness. A later-received frame remains eligible even when its loaded value decreases or resets.
Preserve existing navigation and cleanup behavior across synchronous start, unlisten, cancellation, and host callbacks, including idempotent cancellation and inert repeated removal.

Preserve Retry behavior shown by the public source: cancel the entry visit's previous handle, enqueue one retry for that accepted visit, install it only if that visit remains current, otherwise cancel it, and show its queued notice only while current.
Preserve queue recording before attempt construction, existing payload shapes, session counters, Snapshot behavior, disposal, ordinary streaming, and subsequent reuse.
Leave NewTelemetry behavior unchanged, including start before listen and recordDelta delivery; the panel repair must not alter diagnostic telemetry.

ordering_barriers: For the panel, reception must be capable of observing a cached packet emitted during start.
Reception order must be captured before decode, whose completion may be immediate or deferred.
Existing audit remains before the visible view decision for a completed decode.
Current-visit authority and freshness must be evaluated after audit returns because host callbacks are synchronous unless deferred.
Publication order must be committed before showProgress because showProgress may synchronously navigate or cause other work.
Retry cancellation remains before enqueueing its replacement attempt.
The queue record remains before NewAttempt and transport startup.
Select clears the old current visit before releasing it and rechecks the request after callback-capable release.
Listener retirement and returned-subscription reconciliation must prevent an older startup continuation from taking ownership away from newer navigation.
preservation: The existing deliver sequence remains audit followed by view consideration.
Ordinary later packets continue through the panel subscription after the cached startup packet.
Transfer construction retains the existing file token and attempt number.
Attempt cancellation retains context cancellation, listener stop, and transport cancellation in their existing order.
Retry stays in the same visit and retains one new attempt and queue record when accepted.
Select, Hide, Dispose, Snapshot, session-local counters, and later selection of the same file retain existing observable behavior.
Queue records remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}; queued notices remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, status:"queued"}.
Listener removal remains committed before its synchronous host callback, and repeated removal remains inert.
Telemetry continues recording its existing decoded live deltas without adopting panel bootstrap or display filtering.
No new behavior is specified for rejected decode or physical transfer completion.
scope: The contract covers panel start/listen ordering, callback-capable startup ownership, decode audit/display separation, reception-order display freshness, and lifecycle coordination required to preserve documented behavior.
Retry is included because it replaces an attempt without creating a visit and must retain existing behavior.
Tests, configuration, public interfaces, payload formats, dependencies, and runtime declarations are outside the edit scope.

Decode completions occur in a different order from packet reception.
Retry replaces the physical attempt within the current visit.
Select, Hide, Dispose, recordProgress, showProgress, unlisten, or cancellation synchronously changes lifecycle state.

The public sources do not mandate a particular provisional handle, listener-retirement representation, sequence-counter type, or publication-watermark representation.

No public source supplies frame sequence metadata; reception order is the supported interpretation of frame age.
